conflicts.about: Where the Transport details card's Country comes from.

positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as persistence, overrides the prototype.
The country is worked out from the approval number's prefix, and any other prefix shows 'Not applicable'.
The card shows the country stored on the transporter's address.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling's constraint override wins: the real service holds each transporter's country, so the card shows the stored country. The prefix lookup is a stand-in for data the prototype does not hold.

conflicts.about: Whether a submitted notification's view shows its own answers or the prototype's sample answers.

positions.says: A real persistence constraint overrides the prototype.
The submitted view shows the same canned cattle notification for every journey, with only the reference changed.
The submitted view shows a fixed sample notification's answers instead of those just submitted.
A submitted notification's view renders every recorded answer.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling's persistence override wins: the view shows the notification's own stored answers. The canned answers come from the prototype looking up its static examples by reference.

conflicts.about: Whether the declaration submit checks the notification is complete.

positions.says: A real validation constraint overrides the prototype.
The declaration page does not check completeness and its submit saves the notification as submitted.
The declaration submit re-checks the review's refusal test and sends the trader back to the review if refused.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling's validation override wins for the submit: it keeps today's re-check. The page itself still opens unchecked, as both sources do, so nothing from the prototype is set aside.

conflicts.about: Whether identifier-driven outstanding items (the confirmation bullet, the action-required warnings and error, and the dashboard's 'Information is missing') are built now, and what makes identifiers incomplete.

positions.says: One identifier is enough: DR1 inc-103 is closed and not built, its blocker is removed, and these requirements are weighed against the one-identifier rule.
The identifier bullet stays unbuilt until the design authority rules on inc-103.
Undecided: whether the zero-record single-species case fires the bullet at once or with the rest.
Whether DR1's every-identifier rule or V4's at-least-one rule governs inc-103 is undecided; only the design authority can say.
A notification with required but incomplete identifiers that meets the submission minimum is submitted with the item 'complete the animal identifier information in the notification'.
The confirmation page holds the identifier bullet back on the open identifier-completeness decision.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October ruling ranks first and settles it: an animal record counts as identified once one identifier is filled, inc-103 is closed, and the identifier-driven items are built now with no blocker. Design Release 2.1 settles the rest: identifiers are incomplete when a line whose species asks for identifiers holds fewer identified records than the animals it declares, which includes the single-species consignment with none saved (DR1's p8-062 case). The DR1 hold, its undecided zero-record timing and the notes' open question are set aside. Today's frontend holding the bullet back (repo-frontend-p14-045) is the state that changes, and stays cited as the delta.

conflicts.about: How the review names unfinished commodity and species answers.

positions.says: Each short species gets its own message ('Enter the number of animals for <species>', 'Enter at least 1 animal identifier for <species>'), and incomplete consignment details show 'Complete commodity details'.
Every unfinished commodity, consignment details or identification state shows one 'Complete species details' entry linked to the section heading, marking no card.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype outranks the frontend and wins. DR1 parity row inc-150 deferred species marking for a design ruling (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p8-039) and made no judgement of its own, so Design Release 2.1 supplies the design it waited for. The prototype's anchors (review-species-<n>, #review-commodity-details) name no element, so the links go to the species block and the first commodity card they were meant to reach.

conflicts.about: The duplicate error summary entries when a party's saved address has been deleted.

positions.says: Undecided: whether a deleted-address party error suppresses its card's entry, rewords it, or both entries stay; then pin it with a full-list test.
The error summary has one entry per unfinished card and no deleted-address case.
Party address errors come first in the summary, then the unfinished cards.
Nothing other than a DR1 judgement on the same difference or a real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides the prototype.

conflicts.outcome: The review's error summary follows Design Release 2.1: one entry per unfinished card, each linking to its card. A party whose saved address has been deleted makes the roles and addresses card unfinished, so the summary carries the single 'Complete roles and addresses' entry linking to #roles-and-addresses, and the specific deleted-address message ('Select an address for the consignor') stays on that party's row inside the card. The separate party entry is dropped. Because the card entry stays, a second unanswered role in the same card is never hidden (the concern DR1 row inc-150 raised). A test pins the full error list for a deleted consignor.

conflicts.about: Whether an amendment's review shows errors.

positions.says: A real validation constraint overrides the prototype.
When a notification is being amended the review shows no card errors and no error summary.
An amendment is editable on the review like a draft, with its errors.

conflicts.outcome: Split by what each part needs. The prototype wins for the amendment review on opening: no error summary and no card errors. The ruling's validation override wins when an amendment that is not complete is submitted: Continue is refused and the re-shown review names what is missing, because the real service must not accept it silently.

conflicts.about: The 'Edit details' row actions on party and contact address rows.

positions.says: The prototype wins by default over what the real services do today.
General review card rows have no row-level link; the Addresses card has only its header Change link.
Each answered party row and the contact address row carry an 'Edit details' link to the party edit page.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins: the review drops the row-level 'Edit details' links. The validation route to the edit page stays: a party whose copied address breaks the address-book rules still links from the error summary to its edit page (c-139).

conflicts.about: Review errors that come from real validation the prototype does not show: invalid copied party addresses and stale stored answers.

positions.says: A real validation constraint overrides the prototype.
The review error summary lists only unfinished cards, in a fixed order.
The review names an answered party whose copied address breaks the address-book rules, and stale stored answers, and refuses Continue.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling's validation override wins: these errors and the refusal stay. The prototype's card errors and their order are kept for everything else.

conflicts.about: Document virus-scan errors on the review.

positions.says: Cross-service behaviour the prototype cannot express overrides it.
Uploaded documents never show an error on the review.
A rejected document is named on the Documents card on every visit, and rejected or scanning documents stop Continue.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling's cross-service override wins: scan errors stay. Documents remain optional for submission, as the prototype says.

conflicts.about: How the review links to answers collected on a second page: transit countries and the CPH number.

positions.says: Transit countries sit inside the Arrival details card with their own row-level Change link; the CPH is a row of the Addresses card, reached by its one link.
A card has one Change link to the page the hub's task row leads with; a conditional second page gets its own headed card.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype outranks the frontend and wins. DR1 parity row inc-146 deferred the card structure to a design decision (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p8-047) without judging it, so Design Release 2.1 supplies it: transit countries move into Arrival details with a row Change link, and a CPH change from the Addresses card returns to the review.

conflicts.about: Subsection headings above each review card.

positions.says: Each numbered section holds its cards directly, with no subsection heading.
Every card stands under its own h3 subsection heading.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype outranks the frontend and wins: subsection headings go. DR1 parity row inc-147 added them to match DR1 and left the repeated headings as an open design call (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p8-051); Design Release 2.1 answers it by dropping the subsection headings and keeping the card titles.

conflicts.about: Which dashboard 'Return to your dashboard' and the viewed notification's Back link go to.

positions.says: The view's Back link goes to the overall dashboard at the mount root, even when opened from the live animals list.
The dashboard is temporary in the animals frontend and moves to the INS front door.
'Return to your dashboard' goes to the animals service's base path, /live-animals.
The view's Back link and the confirmation's return link are kept, as c-143 set them.

conflicts.outcome: 'Return to your dashboard' on the confirmation page and a viewed notification's Back link both go to the overall dashboard, which is the INS front door's dashboard (trade-imports-ins-frontend), reached through its configured URL on the workspace stack and in CDP. The prototype sends both links to the overall dashboard (prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-101, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-159) and DR1 already ruled the dashboard moves to the INS front door (document-dr1-parity-notes-p1-014), so today's link to the animals frontend's /live-animals list changes. Where the animals frontend runs without an INS front-door URL configured, the link falls back to /live-animals.

conflicts.about: How the trader completes outstanding items on an action-required notification.

positions.says: A real persistence constraint overrides the prototype.
Opening an action-required notification loads its snapshot into the session as the notification being worked on, and Continue goes to the hub.
Only a SUBMITTED status makes the review read-only; a notification being amended is editable.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling's persistence override wins on the mechanism: the real service changes a submitted notification only through an amendment, so Continue on the action-required view starts an amendment and opens the hub. The prototype's view, warning and Continue-to-hub are kept.

conflicts.about: Which paths and query parameters the review, declaration and confirmation pages use.

positions.says: No increment changes an existing real URL path to match the prototype.
The review is GET /review-notification, keyed by ?submitted= or ?reference=.
The review is served at notification-view under the notification.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: the three pages keep their real paths (notification-view, declaration, confirmation) and the view is keyed on the real route and status. The prototype's paths and query parameters are not built.

conflicts.about: Where a draft's view header applies, now that dashboard draft rows go to the hub.

positions.says: The view header is keyed on the real route and status, and dashboard draft rows keep going to the hub; req-900's content is kept.
A draft opened from the dashboard shows the header with 'Draft' and 'Date created', editable with its errors.
The journey review shows the status strip, the 'Review your notification' heading and a Back link to the hub, with no header.
A draft has one review, at notification-view, reached from the hub.

conflicts.outcome: Open. The ruling keeps the draft view's content but sends dashboard draft rows to the hub, so the only real route to a draft's review is the journey review, which Design Release 2.1 draws without the header. Read one way the draft's review stays the journey review; read the other it gains the header. The two build different pages.
conflicts.question: With dashboard draft rows going to the hub, should a draft's review (reached from the hub's 'Review and submit') stay the journey review, or show the view header with the reference as heading, 'Date created', 'Copy as new', 'Delete' and the Import reference numbers?
conflicts.default: A draft's review stays the journey review: 'Review your notification' heading, Draft status strip and Back link to the hub, editable with its Change links, errors, Continue and Delete (req-820, req-821, req-837, req-872, req-888). The view header, its dates and buttons, and the Import reference numbers show for Submitted, Submitted action required and Completed only. 'Date created', Copy as new and the Import reference numbers on a draft are not built.

conflicts.about: What the confirmation page's 'Create a new notification' does.

positions.says: Create a new notification stays a real mechanism, not a GET start page.
It is a link to the create-notification start page.
It is a link-styled button that posts to the create route and starts a fresh notification on the origin page.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: today's real mechanism stays, looking and reading as Design Release 2.1's link. The prototype's GET link to its start page is not built.

conflicts.about: Whether the declaration page guards against template mode.

positions.says: The prototype's template URL guards are not required.
Opening the declaration while creating a template redirects to the review.
Posting the declaration while creating a template redirects to the review without submitting.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: a template never offers a declaration, because its review ends with 'Save template' (req-941), so the guards are not built.
